entries.title: Job 7:1
segments: ¶Hath not man a life of labour upon earth? and are not his days like the days of a hireling?

entries.title: Job 7:2
segments: As a bondman earnestly desireth the shadow, and a hireling expecteth his wages,

entries.title: Job 7:3
segments: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

entries.title: Job 7:4
segments: If I lie down, I say, When shall I rise up, and the darkness be gone? and I am full of tossings until the dawn.

entries.title: Job 7:5
segments: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and suppurates.

entries.title: Job 7:6
segments: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

entries.title: Job 7:7
segments: ¶Remember thou that my life is wind; mine eye shall no more see good.

entries.title: Job 7:8
segments: The eye of him that hath seen me shall behold me no [more]: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.

entries.title: Job 7:9
segments: The cloud consumeth and vanisheth away; so he that goeth down to Sheol shall not come up.

entries.title: Job 7:10
segments: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him again.

entries.title: Job 7:11
segments: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth: I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

entries.title: Job 7:12
segments: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, that thou settest a watch over me?

entries.title: Job 7:13
segments: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

entries.title: Job 7:14
segments: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions;

entries.title: Job 7:15
segments: So that my soul chooseth strangling, death, rather than my bones.

entries.title: Job 7:16
segments: I loathe it; I shall not live always: let me alone, for my days are a breath.

entries.title: Job 7:17
segments: ¶What is man, that thou makest much of him? and that thou settest thy heart upon him?

entries.title: Job 7:18
segments: And that thou visitest him every morning, triest him every moment?

entries.title: Job 7:19
segments: How long wilt thou not look away from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

entries.title: Job 7:20
segments: Have I sinned, what do I unto thee, thou Observer of men? Why hast thou set me as an object of assault for thee, so that I am become a burden to myself?

entries.title: Job 7:21
segments: And why dost not thou forgive my transgression and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I lie down in the dust, and thou shalt seek me early, and I shall not be.
